# Two accumulators of one limb into one

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `acc_merge_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A step of an accumulator: the running sum $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + v)$, and the sum of the magnitudes $b$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t = \mathrm{RN}(s + v), \qquad b = \mathrm{RN}(a + c).$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A.merge(B)` | `Accumulator<T, 1>`, `Accumulator<T, 1>` | `void` | a node of the summation tree; the counts added |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `A` and `B` are accumulators, `kairn::Accumulator<T, k>`, header `kairn/accumulator.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` includes. They take no marker: an operation of an accumulator compiles only while its kernels are proved ([The accumulator](accumulator.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $a \ge 0$.
- $c \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + v)$: the number of the format nearest to $s + v$, ties to even.
- $\lvert t - (s + v)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert s + v\rvert$.
- $b = \mathrm{RN}(a + c)$: the number of the format nearest to $a + c$, ties to even.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u$ | $\frac{1}{2^{53} + 1} \approx 1.1102 \times 10^{-16}$ | $\frac{1}{2^{24} + 1} \approx 5.9605 \times 10^{-8}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-53`, `0.0` | `0x1p-24f`, `0.0f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1p-53`, `0.0` | `0x1p-24f`, `0.0f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `acc_merge_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/AccKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/AccKernels.v), against `acc_merge_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions acc_merge_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition acc_merge_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s a v c : R,
  fmt emin prec s ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec v ->
  fmt emin prec c ->
  0 <= a ->
  0 <= c ->
  let '(t, b) := acc_merge_1 emin prec tie_even s a v c in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  fmt emin prec b /\
  t = RN emin prec (s + v) /\
  Rabs (t - (s + v)) <= (1 / (1 + u prec)) * u prec ^ 1 * Rabs (s + v) /\
  b = RN emin prec (a + c).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `acc_merge_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** add_1_1 of two running sums, and the sum of the magnitudes (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/acc_merge_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/acc_merge_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# acc.merge(other) of Accumulator<T, 1> (milestone2.md, "The accumulator"): the running sums added,
# as add_1_1 (a node of the tree of the summation), and the sums of the magnitudes added, rounded to
# nearest. The counts are added in the header. Both accumulators are objects: nothing comes from the
# program.

t = add(s, v)
b = add(a, c)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#acc_merge_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

**These runs judged other claims.** They judged `rounded(t) nearest`; `error(t) form R, c=1/(1+u), k=1, t=0`; `rounded(b) nearest of a+c`; the kernel now claims `rounded(t) nearest`; `error(t) form R, c=1/(1+u), k=1, t=0`; `rounded(b) nearest`. Their numbers are not about the statement above.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 98 125 272 | 0 | 1 | yes |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 98 123 778 | 0 | 1 | yes |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 27 416 766 | 0 | 1 (`fp:1:-5:5`) | yes |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
